subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Cut-and-Cover vs. Bored Tunnels
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cut-and-Cover vs. Bored Tunnels.

hook.text: Cut-and-cover is simple: dig a trench, build the tunnel, cover it up. It's cheap but destroys everything on the surface.

buildup.text: London's first underground railway in 1863 used cut-and-cover. Entire streets were torn up, rebuilt, and paved over the tunnel.

discovery.text: Bored tunnels use TBMs to dig deep without disturbing the surface. They cost more but are essential in dense cities.

twist.text: The New Austrian Tunneling Method uses rock as support. Shotcrete and bolts reinforce the natural arch — no full lining needed.

climax.text: Immersed tube tunnels sink prefabricated sections into trenches dug in riverbeds. The sections are joined underwater and drained.

punchline.text: Dig from above, bore from within, or sink from below. Three ways under.

quiz.question: What makes the New Austrian Tunneling Method different from conventional tunneling?
options: It uses explosives instead of boring machines for faster excavation
It uses the surrounding rock as structural support with shotcrete and bolts instead of full lining
It pumps out groundwater before digging to create a dry working environment
